The Story of Jinadatt and Vasumitra

I bow to Lord Jina, who is the originator of Jain dharma, and I write the story of Jinadatt and Vasumitra, who were devoted to the consecration of Lord Jina.

During the reign of King Sagardatt of Ujjain, there lived two famous and very virtuous merchants named Jinadatt and Vasumitra. They had great devotion to Jain dharma and the consecration (abhishek) of Lord Jina. Not a single day passed without their performing the Lord's abhishek, worship, charity, and vows.

One day, both merchants set out from Ujjain to the north for trade. Travelling stage by stage, they entered a dense forest flanked on both sides by mountains — Avisir and Malaparvat — that touched the sky. This was a haunt of bandits. The bandits robbed them of all their goods and disappeared. Now the two merchants wandered here and there in the forest, trying to find a way out. But all their efforts were in vain. Neither could they find the path themselves, nor did they meet anyone who could show them the way.

Seeing no way out of the forest, these great souls, devoted to Jain worship and abhishek, finally took the vow of renunciation and began to remember and contemplate Lord Jina. Truly, the noble always maintain equanimity in happiness and suffering, and remain thoughtful.

Another lost soul, a wandering Brahmin named Somsharma, came upon them in that forest. Seeing the poor Brahmin's condition, they were deeply moved. They told him their whole story and added, 'When we could find no way out despite all efforts, we finally took refuge in dharma. For here, death is our only fate. And since we must face death, why face it with cowardice and evil thoughts, which would lead to a lower birth? Dharma destroys suffering and bestows happiness. Therefore, taking refuge in dharma at such a time is supremely beneficial. We advise you too to take refuge in dharma for the attainment of a good destiny.'

They then explained the general nature of dharma to Somsharma: 'See, those who are free from the eighteen faults and are omniscient, seeing all — they are the true Lords. Their teaching is the true dharma. Those who follow it with faith and conduct attain supreme happiness.'

Through their guidance, Somsharma too took right faith. All three spent their remaining days in meditation and contemplation of the Lord. Through the power of their spiritual practice, they all attained liberation.

This story teaches that in times of complete helplessness, dharma is the only true refuge. Jinadatt and Vasumitra, having lost everything — their wealth, their way, even their hope of survival — turned to the Lord and found peace. Their devotion to Jain worship and abhishek had prepared them for this moment. The wise should cultivate devotion to dharma in good times so that it becomes their refuge in times of crisis.
